From your saved notes:
- Shoulder: Your gym log (entry 10) records squats 5x5 at 80kg and bench 3x8 at 55kg, with the left shoulder "slightly tight" on the last set. That's the only mention — there are no saved stretches, remedies, or reminders for it.
- Dentist: Entry 22 says the appointment was moved to next Tuesday 4pm, and to bring the insurance card.

What to do — shoulder (general knowledge, not from your notes):
- Treat it as a mild signal, not an emergency. It showed up under load at the end of a set, which often points to fatigue, form drift, or a warm-up gap rather than injury.
- Ease off pressing/overhead work briefly rather than pushing through: drop bench volume or weight, and avoid anything that reproduces sharp pain.
- Add easy mobility and light rotator-cuff work: pendulum swings, wall slides, band external rotations, doorway chest stretch. Gentle range of motion beats aggressive stretching.
- Check the basics: warm up shoulders before benching, keep shoulder blades set/retracted, don't let the bar drift too low, and give the area a rest day.
- Heat or ice for comfort is fine; neither fixes a load problem.
- Escalate if it persists beyond about 1–2 weeks, worsens, or comes with pain at rest, numbness/tingling down the arm, weakness, or clicking with pain — that warrants a physio or doctor, not self-management.
- Re-check your log next shoulder session and note whether tightness is earlier, later, or gone; that pattern tells you if the deload worked.

What to do — dentist:
- Put next Tuesday 4pm in your calendar now, with a reminder the day before and a morning-of reminder.
- Confirm the insurance card is physically in your wallet/bag before you leave (that's the one prep item your note calls out).
- Optionally add a short list of anything you want to raise (sensitivity, cleaning, costs) and note travel time so 4pm isn't tight.
- If the move to Tuesday created a conflict with anything else, check your calendar and reschedule early.

- Generics type erasure (नोट 4): List<String> runtime पर सिर्फ़ List रह जाता है, इसलिए instanceof List<String> या new T[] नहीं कर सकते; generic varargs से unchecked warning आता है। जैसे: `if (x instanceof List<String>) {} // compile error`
- Collections (नोट 23): HashMap में एक null key और कई null values चलती हैं; Hashtable में कोई नहीं; HashMap synchronized नहीं है। जैसे: `map.put(null, null); // HashMap में OK`
- Exceptions (नोट 28): checked को declare या catch करना ज़रूरी; unchecked RuntimeException के subclasses हैं; try-with-resources उल्टे क्रम में close करता है। जैसे: `try (var r = open()) { ... }`
- ArrayList vs LinkedList (नोट 3): ArrayList array-backed है इसलिए O(1) random access; LinkedList में get(i) O(n) पर ends पर insert/remove O(1)। नोट में यह भी लिखा है कि DSA exam में आप ये दोनों मिक्स कर देते हैं। जैसे: `list.get(i); // O(1) ArrayList, O(n) LinkedList`
- Spring @Transactional (नोट 17): यह सिर्फ़ proxy के रास्ते काम करता है, self-invocation पर bypass हो जाता है — @Cacheable में भी वही trap। जैसे: `this.doWork(); // @Transactional लागू नहीं होगा`
- Inheritance/Liskov (नोट 5): inheritance code reuse के लिए नहीं, substitutability के लिए है — B is-a A हो तो जहाँ A चलता है वहाँ B भी चलना चाहिए (LSP), और LSP chapter दोबारा पढ़ना है। (ध्यान दें: इस नोट में 'जावा' शब्द सीधे नहीं लिखा, यह उसी स्टडी क्लास का OOP नोट है।)

But two pairs pull in different directions, and one is worth an explicit reconciliation.

Tensions worth reconciling

- Default tracking vs. a privacy toggle (notes 2 and 13). Note 2 says the system will track "all kinds of data of the user by default" and use that context to organize info. Note 13 says the tracking-by-default idea "needs a privacy toggle." These are not logically incompatible (default-on with an opt-out satisfies both), but the design stance shifts from "capture everything by default" to "capture, but give the user a control." Treat this as a revised decision unless you actually meant default-on plus a toggle.

- Semantic retrieval vs. embeddings deferred (notes 18 and 24). Note 18 records the project goal as a DBMS for personal notes that supports semantic retrieval, not just keyword search. Note 24 records the meeting decision with Arjun that retrieval will be lexical plus graph, with embeddings deferred to v2. Semantic retrieval is normally embeddings-based, so the v1 design as written cannot be fully semantic. This reads as a scope/phase difference (v1 = lexical + graph, semantic later) rather than a true contradiction — but if "semantic retrieval" was meant as the unqualified goal for the first version, then notes 18 and 24 do conflict and you should pick one.

Minor, within a single note

- Note 20: "argue with you about them" vs. "form opinions about them." That is self-revision inside one draft, not a cross-note contradiction.

Checked and consistent

- Java notes 3, 4, 23, and 17 agree with each other: ArrayList O(1) random access vs. LinkedList O(n) get(i) with O(1) end operations; type erasure behavior; HashMap allowing one null key and multiple null values while Hashtable allows neither; the @Transactional / @Cacheable self-invocation proxy trap. No conflicts there.
- Note 29 (spaced repetition over interpretations, with the "concepts too broad" risk) and note 30 (wanting to see which notes were used, not just cited ids) conflict with nothing in this set.
- Note 25 (Pune train, 5th out, 7th return) is standalone and unrelated to the rest.

One scoping note: per your own guidance, note 18 is your DeepNotes DBMS college project, not Java coursework — so the semantic-vs-embeddings tension in the second bullet belongs to the project track and should be kept out of Java study material.
